support.locus: Tab. Iguv. VIa (repeated prayer: ... nerf arsmo ueiro pequo castruo fri salua seritu)

cognate: Ved. paśú- = Av. pasu- = Umbr. pequo = Lat. pecu < *péḱu 'livestock'; Ved. vīrá- = Av. vīra- = Umbr. ueiro (Lat. vir) < *wiHró- 'man'
drift_or_renewal: Latin (Cato's lustration prayer) renews *wiHro- with pastores while keeping pecua; word order varies: Indo-Iranian 'cattle + men', Italic 'men + cattle'
shared_syntax: a fixed two-member pair (asyndetic in Av. pasu vīra, Umbr. ueiro pequo; with ca in AVP paśubhiś ca vīraiḥ) as object or instrument of a verb of keeping or furthering welfare: Av. fradaϑāi (Y45.9), amaršaṇta 'did not die' (Y9.4), Ved. bhavāsi / saṃ bhavāsi 'thrive' with paśubhiś ca vīraiḥ, Umbr. salua seritu 'keep safe', Lat. salua seruassis
context: Every witness is a blessing or prayer for the household's or community's prosperity: AVP 19.56 is an oblation refrain (te haviṣā juhomi ... bhavāsi paśubhiś ca vīraiḥ), and the context line of s26 adds the 'four-footed and two-footed' merism; Y45.9 asks Mazda to further 'our cattle and men'; Y9.4 describes Yima's golden age, when cattle and men did not die; VS10.18 is the purified 'cattle and men' of the land. Umbrian and Latin use it in lustration prayers. The domain matches (welfare of people and livestock under divine protection), the pairing is fixed (not just two co-occurring common nouns), and it recurs as a unit in four traditions, so chance is unlikely. Note: the OE partners in these bundles are false matches (OCR 'fe6wer' = feower 'four' mis-mapped to feoh and wer) and give no evidence.
phrase: Av. pasu vīra / Ved. paśubhiś ca vīraiḥ / Umbr. ueiro pequo 'cattle and men' (Lat. pastores pecuaque)

note: Slab is dominated by repetitive Vendidad formulas paired with unrelated Greek prose. One cross-branch claim: paśu/vīra (cattle and men). Checked and not claimed: Y62.6c vaŋhāuca srauuahi 'good fame' (B-cc75b) against the slab's Greek κλέος/εὐκλεής passages (Aesch. Epigr. 7.255.3 in B-86e68, Hdt 7.228.3 in B-ad23e, Plato Symp. 208d ctx in B-2e043). vaŋhu- is not cognate with εὐ-, the Greek is prose or epigram with no matching collocation, so I would not defend it. Parallels within Indic only, not claimed: AVP 19.52.1 ~ RV 9.74.4 (nábhaḥ ... páyaḥ, ṛtásya nā́bhir amṛ́tam); AVP 19.55.3 manasā/hṛdayena ~ RV 10.10.13. The 'two-footed and four-footed' merism (AVP 19.56.s26 context; Umbr. dupursus peturpursus) has only one branch in the slab, so it is not claimed separately.
